newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes higher on weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes higher on weather concerns.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher on concerns about how wet, cold weather will impact the northern U.S. Plains spring wheat seeding, traders said.
"We do have water problems in the Red River Valley and there could be record floods," a trader said.
The wet and cold weather, including additional snowfall over the weekened, led to concerns about delays in seeding the U.S. spring wheat crop.
"They were ready to go (seeding) west of the Red River Valley and the big weather came in again," a trader said.
Traders said the harsh weather would delay spring wheat seedings by up to two weeks.
MGE spring wheat futures closed 12-1/2 to 14-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with May up 14-1/2 at $4.11-1/2.
MGE estimated wheat futures volume for Monday was 29,762 contracts, slightly above the 23,722 traded Friday.
After the close, USDA reported U.S. spring wheat seeding was one percent complete as of Sunday, the same as a year ago but modestly behind three percent for the five-year average.
Barley futures closed unchanged to 0.60 cents per cwt higher, with May unchanged at $6.61 per cwt.
